plain_description.what: On the multi-benchmark union data, with training and evaluation sides split so no question text is shared, it picks the best overall model and a per-cell challenger on the training side. It then checks on the evaluation side, cell by cell, whether the challenger really beats the overall best beyond noise. The tree is built separately inside each source benchmark, so it uses the source label (source-conditioned) and is not fully label-free. No judge calls; answer keys only.
plain_description.why: Tests the core premise of cell-conditional evaluation: do some cells of the tree have a different best model than the global leaderboard says?
plain_description.information: If no cell flips, reporting per cell adds nothing over one leaderboard. If cells flip, it does add something. Result: flips exist. 7 of 101 tested cells show a real winner change (4.6% of items), mostly reasoning-puzzle (BBH) task cells won by one model. This is the same reordering the declared task labels already show. It does not show that the tree finds order changes the labels miss (3 such flips are descriptive only), nor that BBH as a whole has a different winner. One data draw only.
